notes:
CIRCUIT: a three-node ladder on a single grounded bottom rail. V-DC #5 (100V, '+' up / '-' down) drives R#1 (10Kohm) in series along the top; R#6 (40Kohm) shunts to ground at the midpoint; L#0 (17mH) carries on to the right-hand node, where I-DC #4 (0.3A, arrow up), C#2 (2F) and I-DC #3 (7A, arrow up) all shunt to ground. GND #7 hangs off the bottom rail at x~486. The heavy rectangle around the page is a drawing frame, not a wire, and is correctly excluded from every net.

NET MAP
  0  = the bottom rail, y~625..635, running from (170,632) under the voltage source east to (900,625) under the 7A source: bottom of V-DC #5, bottom of R#6, bottom of I-DC #4, bottom of C#2, bottom of I-DC #3, and GND #7's stem at (486,643). 6 terminals.
  n3 = top of V-DC #5 -> up the short lead from (141,463) to the corner at (133,408) -> east along y~406 to the left end of R#1 at (213,405). Just those 2 terminals; nothing else reaches this segment.
  n1 = right end of R#1 (320,410) -> east along y~406 -> top of R#6 joining at S3 (374,406) -> on to the left end of L#0 at (444,401). Terminals: 1.1, 6.0, 0.0.
  n2 = right end of L#0 (565,404) -> east along y~399, picking up the top lead of I-DC #4 at S2 (604,403) and the top lead of C#2 at S1 (738,399) -> continues to (900,390) and down into the top of I-DC #3. Terminals: 0.1, 4.0, 2.0, 3.1.

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITES - every CRITICAL site here is an unambiguous T; none needed an override, and each explicit key records that it was inspected on its 5x crop:
  * S3 (374,406) JUNCTION - R#6's top lead rises and terminates on the upper rail, which runs straight through east-west. Nothing above the rail here, so 'crossing' is not even a legal reading: it would strand R#6's top terminal on a 1-terminal net with no return path.
  * S2 (604,403) JUNCTION - same shape for I-DC #4's top lead onto the upper rail.
  * S1 (738,399) JUNCTION - same shape for C#2's top lead. The rail is drawn in two pen strokes that abut at the node (left stroke ends at x=738, right stroke restarts at x~747), which is why the crop looks slightly broken; the tracer resolved all three branches at one site and the drawing plainly intends one node.
  * S9 (388,628) JUNCTION - R#6's bottom lead descends onto the bottom rail (dot score 2.0, visible ink thickening).
  * S10 (628,632) JUNCTION - I-DC #4's bottom lead descends onto the bottom rail (dot 2.5, the clearest node blob on the sheet).
  * S8 (758,627) JUNCTION - C#2's bottom lead descends onto the bottom rail. This only became netlist-critical after the port fix on #2 below; the crop shows a clean corner-into-T with the rail continuing both sides.
  * S12 (484,634) JUNCTION - GND #7's stem drops off the bottom rail. Reported as deg=4 because the very short stub edge is counted twice; the hop score of 2.1 is just the small vertical kink where the hand-drawn rail restarts, not a hop arc (there is no second wire here to hop over). A ground symbol must connect, so junction is forced.
  * Non-critical, left at default: S5 (796,470) is the '2F' label brushing the capacitor box; S6 (956,514) is the '7A' label; S7 (103,523) is the 'V' of '100V'. None affects the netlist.
  There are NO wire-over-wire crossings anywhere on this sheet - every intersection is a T - and no hop or jog is drawn anywhere.

PORT / PIN FIXES - the tracer put three terminals on handwritten value-label strokes, producing three 1-terminal nets (n4, n5, n6) plus a stranded n3:
  * #2 Capacitor t1: was p2@(790,458), a stroke of the '2F' label to the right of the symbol (2-px and 21-px stubs, p3/p2). The real bottom plate lead is p0@(749,503), a 122-px run down to the bottom rail at S8. Repointed t1 -> p0, which puts it on net 0.
  * #3 I-DC (7A) t1: was p3@(950,514), a 3-px fragment of the '7A' label. The real top lead is p1@(897,457), a 65-px run up to the corner at (900,390) on the upper-right rail. Repointed t1 -> p1, which puts it on n2.
  * #5 V-DC (100V) t0: was p2@(106,512), a 9-px stroke of the 'V' in the '100V' label at the left of the symbol. The real top lead is p1@(141,463), a 53-px run up to the corner at (133,408). Repointed t0 -> p1. inkmap at (133,410) confirms that corner is solid continuous ink joining the vertical to the y~406 horizontal, so this also cured the stranded n3 (R#1's left terminal) by giving it its partner.
  * Verified and left alone: #0 (p0 left / p1 right), #1 (p0 left / p1 right; p2 is '10Kohm' ink), #4 (p1 top / p0 bottom; p2,p3 are '0.3A' ink), #6 (p0 top / p1 bottom; p2 is '40Kohm' ink), #7 GND (p0 stem).

CLASSES: all correct. #3 and #4 are current sources (circles with vertical arrows, '7A' and '0.3A'); #5 is a voltage source (circle with '+' over '-', '100V'); #1 and #6 are zig-zag resistors; #0 is a coil; #2 is a two-plate capacitor. No 3-terminal parts, so no pin-order risk.
UNRESOLVED: none. ERC clean, 8 components, 4 nets.
